                    ### Question

On physical examination, there is diffuse nontender enlargement of the thyroid gland. Fine-needle aspiration and cytology show lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers and epithelial Hürthle cells. Which of the following autoantibodies is most likely to be found in this patient?

                    ### Options

opc. Antihistone antibody
opd. Antimitochondrial antibody
ope. Anti-parietal cell antibody

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a patient with diffuse nontender enlargement of the thyroid gland, lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers, and epithelial Hürthle cells, Hashimoto's thyroiditis is suspected. The most likely autoantibody to be found in this patient is antimicrosomal antibody (anti-thyroid peroxidase antibody), as it is commonly associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
